3.99

ORICE MAGIE POATE FI FOLOSITĂ PENTRU LUCRURI MĂREȚE SAU TERIBILE

Trinity Marrow pierde bătălia și pe Protectorul ei drag. Acum, chiar dacă îi are de partea ei pe demoni și pe Gardieni, nu e sigur că va câștiga lupta împotriva Mesagerului.

Aducerea lui Lucifer înapoi în lume pentru a doborî această entitate malefică probabil că nu e cea mai grozavă idee, dar pare unica soluție... așa cum doar ultimul înger căzut rămas, cu imensa lui putere, poate redresa cursul evenimentelor. În vreme ce între Trin și Zayne se creează o nouă și mult mai periculoasă legătură, Lucifer coboară iadul pe Pământ, și la orizont se întrevede amenințătoarea apocalipsă. Lumea se află pe buza prăpastiei, sfârșitul e iminent și nu există decât o singură certitudine: fie că forțele Binelui vor învinge sau nu, nimic nu va mai fi ca înainte.

Pasiune, trădare, greșeli mortale... trilogia Mesagerul se încheie cu un roman animat de personaje memorabile, de scene imprevizibile și de un sfârșit dulce-amar care îi va emoționa pe cititori.



„Ca de obicei, Armentrout excelează în crearea unei lumi paranormale credibile, accesibile și încântătoare.“ – Booklist

About the author

Jennifer L. Armentrout

To email me, please use the below addy.
jenniferlarmentrout@live.com

# 1 New York Times and # 1 International Bestselling author Jennifer lives in Charles Town, West Virginia. All the rumors you’ve heard about her state aren’t true. When she’s not hard at work writing. she spends her time reading, watching really bad zombie movies, pretending to write, hanging out with her husband and her Jack Russell Loki. In early 2015, Jennifer was diagnosed with retinitis pigmentosa, a group of rare genetic disorders that involve a breakdown and death of cells in the retina, eventually resulting in loss of vision, among other complications. Due to this diagnosis, educating people on the varying degrees of blindness has become of passion of hers, right alongside writing, which she plans to do as long as she can.

Her dreams of becoming an author started in algebra class, where she spent most of her time writing short stories….which explains her dismal grades in math. Jennifer writes young adult paranormal, science fiction, fantasy, and contemporary romance. She is published with Tor, HarperCollins Avon and William Morrow, Entangled Teen and Brazen, Disney/Hyperion and Harlequin Teen. Her Wicked Series has been optioned by PassionFlix. Jennifer has won numerous awards, including the 2013 Reviewers Choice Award for Wait for You, the 2015 Editor’s Pick for Fall With Me, and the 2014/2015 Moerser-Jugendbuch- Jury award for Obsidian. Her young adult romantic suspense novel DON’T LOOK BACK was a 2014 nominated Best in Young Adult Fiction by YALSA. Her adult romantic suspense novel TILL DEATH was a Amazon Editor’s Pick and iBook Book of the Month. Her young adult contemporary THE PROBLEM WITH FOREVER is a 2017 RITA Award Winner in Young Adult Fiction. She also writes Adult and New Adult contemporary and paranormal romance under the name J. Lynn. She is published by Entangled Brazen and HarperCollins.

She is the owner of ApollyCon and The Origin Event, the successful annual events that features over hundred bestselling authors in Young Adult, New Adult, and Adult Fiction, panels, parties, and more.

It's like every book in this series got worse and worse🤚 Thank god I'm done.


***There are no spoilers in this review***


It's hilarious looking at 2019 me who absolutely loved the first book, even going as far to say that it was the best book ever. *wheezing* That review embarrasses me immensely and I'm like 95% sure that if I reread Storm and Fury right now, I'd hate it.


Reading this book was such a slog. Literally how I felt with Rage and Ruin... I don't know why I was expecting this to be better than that. It was just worse.🤡 And I have no idea if this is because I'm in a slump, but sooo many things irritated me and it's either that I truly didn't notice all of that in the first two books or JLA just really made this book alone terrible.

Trinity and Zayne annoyed me so much in Rage and Ruin I didn't think it was possible for them to get worse but it was. For one thing, the dialogue was just super cringey, I died many times throughout the book. I can't believe I'm saying this but I was sick of the romance. Like please, how cringey could you get??


Also the obsession with Trinity calling Zayne 'good' every single moment like okay?? Stop?? I get it?? You legit don't need to constantly remind me that Zayne is 'good' or 'perfect'.

And not only would be she saying how "good" Zayne is, but also how he always just said the right things. I swear to god, it was torture. I wanted to kill something. Like actually, the temptation to light this book on fire. unfortunately i couldnt do that since this is a library book

I squeezed my eyes shut. “Why do you always have to say such perfect
things?” (pg220)

“There you go again, saying all the right things,” I murmured. (pg227)

I took a small breath. “That was also the right thing to say.” (pg228)

“Why?” I toppled forward, dropping my head on his shoulder. “Why do you have to always say the right stuff, Zayne?" (pg263)

I pressed my lips together in a mulish line. “You’re doing it again.”
“Doing what?”
“Saying the right stuff.” (pg264)

“Why do you have to be so good? I would be peeking at everyone’s soul every chance I got.” (pg321)

“You’re doing it again.”
“Doing what?”
“Being perfect.” (pg333)

No but like PLEASE STOP I GET IT.

I want to murder these two with my bare hands.🙂 There was this one scene where someone calls Trinity "trifling" and Zayne goes and says he wants to kill said person?? Just um, okay chill dude. Zayne can go die.


Ah, the times when I used to actually be cheering for Zayne and Trin *laughs* I literally despise the two and the romance was the worst part.

Edit: Well yeah never mind as you can see I dropped it to a 1 star anyways. The only reason this doesn't get 1 star is because of Cayman. I'd love to say it was also because of Roth but like JLA totally just erased him from this book until the end... the one demon prince of hell who actually made this series interesting. It's like the friendship that was building up between Trinity and Roth—completely gone.

And like not only did the characters annoy me a lot, but please JLA at least make the story engaging. 503 pages and all I felt was boredom the whole time. Bad characters and dull plot = torture💀 I regret all my life decisions that led me to reading this.


I actually would've given this book 5 stars if both Trinity and Zayne died, but of course that would never happen—at least that would've made this interesting.

End Times!



The following ratings are out of 5:
Narration: 🎧🎧🎧🎧🎧
Romance: 💋💋💋💋💋
Heat/Steam: 🔥🔥
Story/Plot: 📙📕📗📙📙
World building: 🌎🌏🌍🌎
Character development: 👨🏻👱🏻‍♀️🧔🏻👱🏼‍♂️

One thing I really like about Jennifer L. Armentrout books is the fact that she pretty much explains everything that happened in previous books as well as all the different characters and connections instead of just presuming that the reader recently read the prior books in the series.

I did listen to these three books right after each other. However, it is nice for people that either read them right after each are published and wait between books or skip one of the books in the series. I wish more authors would do that. I don’t know how many times I have read a book and forgotten much of what was in the previous book.

The same narrator did this entire series and I really enjoyed her. The storylines were fantastic. Though one story persisted throughout this three book series, each book had its own separate storylines as well. This one had a lot more humor than the other two. I absolutely loved Lucifer and the way he got all caught up in watching Lucifer on Supernatural.



I have to admit though that the story moved a bit slow in the first half of the book. However, once Lucifer came on the scene it did pick up. Trinity and Zayne went through a whole new set of trials and tribulations and had all the love and chemistry of a great romance. I missed Trinity’s ghost friend Peanut through much of this book, but he showed back up not long after Lucifer for some great comic relief as well.

Honestly, I stuck with this book for the characters, who I previously liked. The plot, however, was convoluted and nonsensical, the twist at the end felt like the author retconned her way out of this. Everything was made to fit too neatly.

A large part of this book was dedicated to Zayne and Trinity’s relationship arc, which I preferred to the plot beats when it comes down to it, but their heart-to-hearts were overdone, too sugary sweet. It occurred to me that I might be part of the problem; maybe I’ve outgrown YA to a certain degree, but then again I did enjoy the first two books more than this. Zayne and Trinity were characters I was able to root for – here their relationship started to annoy me.

The dialogue was hit-or-miss for me; sometimes I chuckled, sometimes I rolled my eyes at the forced pop culture humor to it all, especially when it broke up fight scenes, taking away from the urgency and danger of any given situation. And as much as I enjoyed “Supernatural”, this felt like a long advertisement for the show.

All in all, not even GraphicAudio could save this for me, which is a tragedy. I actually abandoned the dramatized adaptation at some point in favor of the ebook so I could get this over with faster. A truly disappointing end to this trilogy. The fact that I reread books 1 and 2 so I could finally read this and enjoy it as a GraphicAudio production just makes me sad.

I want to return to the beginning for a moment; I need to backtrack to make a point about the convoluted plot.

After the cliffhanger in book 2, this book picks up where we left off. Unfortunately, however, we are then treated to one of the worst info dumps ever on all things gargoyles and angels. And the rules didn’t even make sense.

So Zayne has been made an angel upon his death because he is worthy or some shit, but he chose to Fall to be with Trinity and, naturally, in the process everything goes wrong: he not only he forgets Trinity, but he is also exposed to the seven sins and he was witness to humanity’s sins in general, he is further exposed to the anger and bitterness of all those who Fell before him. Also, his senses were “overloaded” and he was “infected” so if he remains in that state he will be more prone to “violence that is seeping into every pore”, becoming a danger to all, essentially “becoming something as vile and evil as any demon.” Oookay then. Like I said, things get convoluted and don’t make much sense, to me anyway.

And I don’t even want to get into the fact that Peanut the ghost, the comic relief, turned out to be an archangel and Trin’s father to boot! What the hell!

Also, one bond between Trin and Zayne is cut by his death only to be replaced by another bond no one knows of until Trinity dies. Actually, as long as he lives, she lives, which is convenient since she would have died otherwise and since Zayne is immortal now as a Fallen angel..

Ok, I’m done. Moving on.

4/5 ★★★★☆

“You are all I ever wanted, even before I knew what I wanted. It was you. It was always you.”

Marathoning this trilogy was one of the best decisions of my year. It was exactly what I needed to read now. Although Grace and Glory was my least favorite of the three, I find these books up to the mark and totally worth it.



As I said, this third book was my least favorite in the trilogy, since there were several things that did not convince me. However, I really enjoyed this story and consider The Harbinger to be a far better trilogy than The Dark Elements. The characters had a good arc of development and the plot, in general, was well managed.

While this book wasn't perfect and the romance outweighed fantasy, I'll give it four stars because it was still as addictive as ever and made me enjoy it. Sometimes that's all we need from a book. Nonetheless, I understand why some people ended up disappointed, as some characters here feel very different compared to the previous two.

As for the ending, it wasn't quite what I expected. I liked the closure of some things, but others disappointed me a bit. After reading nine of the author's books, I noticed a pattern that she's repeating in all her stories, which lessens the emotion of the book and is no longer surprising. I wish this ending was different, but it didn't ruin the story for me either.

━━━━━•❃°•°•°•°❃•━━━━━

Spoilers ahead:

This section will have some major spoilers for the book, so if you haven't read Grace and Glory yet, don't continue.

1. Peanut was always Michael: I had to start with this because there is too much to discuss about it. On one hand, I liked the idea that Trinity always had her father there with her and I really appreciated that last conversation they both had, she deserved it. However, I can't help but feel like this was forced, almost as if the author hadn't planned it and decided to include it at the last minute. I mean, Peanut was after her daughter's boyfriend... it's not even funny 🥴

“You, a child of one of the most powerful archangels, have always lacked faith.” The Throne smiled at me. “It is a good thing that neither God nor your father have ever lacked faith in you.”

That was nice and I loved it, although I still don't know what to think about this revelation.

2. The subplot of recovering Zayne: This is one of the things that didn't convince me. It is true that everything is resolved relatively quickly, but it seemed unnecessary to me. I would have preferred the book to focus more on the Harbinger, seeing all the threat he posed, than on getting him back after he had this period of "amnesia".

3. The new friendship between Dez and Trinity: While I found it sweet that the clan was so supportive of Trinity, it doesn't change that many things seemed to come out of nowhere.

Dez had only had a few short conversations with her and suddenly he's ready to protect her with his life. We couldn't justify this with his close friendship with Zayne either because the truth is that they didn't even grow up together, they weren't that close, so why was he willing to die to bring him back? He has a wife and children! It's very unrealistic that he would put himself in that situation. It was a forced friendship. Then it got fixed a bit, that's the positive.

4. Zayne's new attitude: I don't know if it's just me, but I feel like the Zayne we see in this book is different from the one we knew before. Yes, he still had his full cinnamon roll moments that made me adore him and kept him on my list of bookish boyfriends, but he definitely changed. It may have been an intentional thing of the author with this whole Falling issue, but sometimes his extreme arrogance just didn't fit the character.

P.S. I still love him, just to make it clear.

5. Tony's appearance: It was short, but I wanted to mention it because I loved it 😆

6. Roth disappears until near the ending of the book: This has me outraged. I imagine JLA replaced Roth with Dez (which didn't work) to prevent fans from pairing our beloved demon prince with Trinity, but this was too sudden. In the first two books, he was constantly appearing and forming a nice friendship with Trin, why couldn't we see more of that?



“You can do it.” Roth bent at the waist and leaned against the counter. “I believe in you.”
“Shut up.”
His golden eyes glimmered with amusement as he looked up at me. “Rude.”

At least their interactions were entertaining, but I insist that I would have liked to see more of the friendship between him and Trinity.

7. Trinity and Cayman's friendship: I appreciate that JLA left us Cayman. His friendship with Trin was hilarious and I think it was well developed, so I really liked it.

“Call me if the spell somehow doesn’t contain him and you need to run for your life,” he’d told me. “I’ll run with you.”

Mental reminder: Get a friend who runs for his life with you 🤣

8. Danika and Nikolai being very cute: If the author decides to write a new trilogy about them, I'll sign up.

This new side of Danika was very entertaining to read, although I would have liked her participation to be greater. Her idea with the gemstones at the end was a waste of time because it's something we never quite finished seeing, which is somewhat disappointing. However, I liked the brief appearances with both.

9. The Crone being Zayne's fan: I really liked the role she played in this book, and the fact we get to know her a little more. Although the cherry on the cake was seeing her flattering Zayne 😂 She will have to compete with Bambi and Cayman for the #1 spot in his fan club.



10. The false pregnancy alarm: NO! This is a great, great NO.

First of all, I don't understand what the "mystery" was as to whether the Trueborn were fertile when it was clear from the beginning that they are. Didn't humans who can see ghosts have an angel in their family tree? To get to the next several generations, there first had to have been a Trueborn and from there come the other descendants. Where was the mystery? But beyond that, I didn't like at all how they concentrated on that topic, they didn't seem like themselves 😬

11. Zayne and Trinity threatening Lucifer: Oh, I loved this 🥳 They were willing to threaten the Devil himself to protect the other, that was beautiful. Also, Roth was the voice of reason right then, and that was a show 😆

12. Zayne lost his soul: Does this mean that he will go to Hell if he is killed? 😲

13. Zayne and Trinity being super cheesy: I know some didn't like this, and it's completely true that they were super cheesy, but I loved seeing them like that.

“I still can’t believe you Fell for me.”
“The Glory was nothing compared to your love.”



“You know I’m always going to be here. Remember? I’ll always be here to make sure you can see the stars. I’m just your Guide...Fallen Angel.”

They are too cute, and I adore them 🥰 I will miss them feeling the emotions of the other.

14. Ghost villains: I didn't like this very much. Gabriel literally appeared briefly only once before the ending and Bael hadn't appeared since Storm and Fury. It was disappointing because Gabriel didn't feel like a real threat and Bael died as soon as he appeared in the ending, without actually doing anything other than summoning fire for three seconds.

15. Jada's return: I wish her appearance was longer, but I still appreciate her return. Trinity needed to have her friends with her and not continue to be left out, having only her boyfriend's friends.

16. Is Thierry Jada's father?: At first I thought it was my mistake and that I had been reading the first two books wrong, but then I realized that I wasn't the only one. He was supposed to be Jada's uncle, so why do they suddenly say he's her father? These types of mistakes make me think that I know the book more than the author herself because it wasn't the only one.

It's a shame neither he nor Matthew showed up again. They were important in Trinity's life, and it would have been nice if they were there for her, even on call or something.

17. Roth WITH horns: As far as I know, in all the books in this universe created by JLA, one of the few differences between gargoyles and demons (skin color aside) is that demons don't have horns while that the Wardens do. So why did Roth get horns this time? 😐

18. Teller's betrayal: It happened really fast, and this character had only appeared once before all this, so I still don't know what to think about that.

19. Zayne and Roth being buddies: This is something I loved from the first book, their rare friendship makes my day and I wanted to highlight it.

“But it warms my heart to know that you care.”
Roth smirked. “Whatever, Stony.”
“You missed me.” Zayne grinned. “Admit it.”



20. Trinity's immortality: Definitely a recycled element from the author because she already used it in Every Last Breath with Layla and in The Crown of Gilded Bones with Poppy. It was all very convenient, and while I like the idea that she and Zayne can live their happily ever after, I would have preferred this to be handled differently.

Positive point was that Trinity continued with her vision problems instead of recovering it as if by magic.

21. The new bond: I understand the concept, but there's something that I don't quite understand. If this bond is stronger than the Protector's, then why does Trinity keep getting weaker when using her grace? That didn't happen to her when she was tied to Zayne and he was a Warden. I'm curious.

22. Zayne being a cinnamon roll for the millionth time: I couldn't finish this review without mentioning this 🤣 There's a beautiful scene that I had to include.

“Did I ever tell you what Heaven smelled like to me?”
I lifted my head, searching to find his features in the dim light. “No, you didn’t.”
“Jasmine,” he said. “Heaven smelled like jasmine.”
It took me a moment—okay, it probably took longer than it should for me to get that, but then I did. “My body wash is jasmine.”
“I know,” he confirmed. “Heaven smelled like you.”



23. A spin-off for Lucifer: I really liked reading him in this book, so I'm signing up for more 🙋

━━━━━•❃°•°•°•°❃•━━━━━

At the end of all, I liked this book and the romance completely conquered me. That is all there's to say. I highly recommended this trilogy.

━━━━━•❃°•°•°•°❃•━━━━━

Es increible como no importa que seres sobrenaturales aparezcan en las novelas de Jennifer L. Armentrout, siempre capta mi interes y lo que es aun mas impactante, siempre consigue que me enamore de sus personajes.

Grace And Glory es el cierre a una trilogia que recuerdo inicie indecisa, no podia creer que la historia de Zayne fuera a gustarme tanto como lo hizo la de Roth y Layla, imaginen mi cara cuando despues de un par de capitulos de Storm And Fury ya no podia soltar el libro mas de un par de horas, y la misma situacion se dio luego con la siguiente parte y con esta ultima.

Como cierre es bastante increible, me gusto como se desenvolvio la trama, eso si, tengo algunos peros que señalar. Extrañe que no hubiese mas accion, no es que la lectura carezca de escenas trepidantes y de suspenso, es simplemente que yo espere que hubiese mas momentos de tension.

Otro punto que creo que pudo ser mas impactante fue la solucion al " gran problema ", no fue una mala resolucion, fue mas bien que se desarrollo a un ritmo muy rapido y eso le resto sorpresa.

Por lo demas, fue una lectura potente, intrigante, adictiva y muy amena de leer, me encanto especialmente leer las escenas de todos los personajes reunidos, sin importar si eran angeles, demonios, guardianes o fantasmas.

En cuanto al romance, fue todo lo que imaginaba, Trin y Zayne son adorables en este ultimo tomo, eso si, el que no haya un epilogo fue una decepcion, yo necesitaba un epilogo pasado un tiempo.

En conclusion, Grace And Glory es un final ideal para una trilogia muy memorable, lo disfrute como una niña pequeña con juguete nuevo, ahora solo me queda esperar a octubre por la publicacion de A Shadow In The Ember, la espera se me hara larga.

((this review will have a lot of writing errors, english is not my first language and i'm tired))

This book was a disaster. Seriously, it even took me over 40 days to finish it.
I honestly don't know where to start. I'm so exhausted that i highly doubt it will become the long, poisonous review i had planned to write. Although well, knowing me, maybe it is a bit long because brevity is not my thing.
I want to start by saying that i was Team Zayne in 2014 (if you read the main trilogy, you will understand), and that since then, i have waited with a lot of excitement and anxiety that Zayne could star in his own trilogy. And that Jla fulfilled my dreams and expectations in 2019 when he published Storm and Fury and that everything went to hell with its sequel, Rage and Ruin. And when I say that everything went to hell, I mean that I literally threw up from fucking rage. And it is all, and nothing less, Zayne's fault. Because if Zayne wasn't a fucking asshole with no emotional responsibility, I wouldn't be writing this shit right now. But hey, let's not get sidetracked, I don't want to think about the second book because it brings back bad memories and a bad headache.
So it's pretty obvious that my dislike for Zayne wasn't going to allow me to continue with the third book, and I certainly wasn't in my plans, but I couldn't stop thinking about Trinity, my second favorite heroine (after Penryn) and what,,,, i didn't want to die one day without knowing how his story ended, you know?
So I went expecting this book to be a disappointment and of course, i was not wrong LOOOL
I will try to summarize it, but it took me so long to read the whole story that I probably forget a lot of unpleasant details that I will add as the days go by (or not, I really hope to forget about this book as soon).

1. The absence of Roth.
Let's talk about how Jla used Roth's presence in all of the promo teasers for this trilogy and the boy was practically getting more scenes than Zayne and Trinity put together, to mysteriously disappear him in the final conclusion. And I say mysteriously because I feel like Jla killed him and revived him shortly before bringing him back to the third book. The Roth we met was nothing like the Roth from Grace and Glory. He looked like an ugly cheap knockoff. He wasn't Roth and I really disliked that.
Plus there's the fact that I was never a fan of Roth in the main trilogy of his, but I certainly LOVED him in this trilogy, and I came to be hopeful about seeing him more in this book because he was pretty much the star of the previous two books.
So, I can't believe JLA used Roth's presence as the "hero" in the first and second books and almost explored a friendship between Roth and Trinity, for both of them to carry the trilogy on their shoulders because Zayne was as interesting as an old shoe.
And in the last book Jla made Roth barely have a scenes because apparently she didn't want Roth to keep stealing Zayne's limelight. Uhm, too late girl. Two books late. Too late to make that decision. We readers fell in love with Roth and now we wanted to see him!

2. Roth and Trinity's friendship.
In the first book Roth and Trinity teased each other. In the second book they began to spend a lot of time together on "work" issues and a friendship blossomed there. To the point that we could tell that Roth seriously cared about her. They literally went from "I hate you" to "hey I like you" and it was so fantastic that a lot of readers just wished Roth and Trinity would become best friends. Because, whyyy not? Everything indicated that in the third book they could officially consecrate their friendship. We were crying out for it.
It includes Cayman as well, who they had a good time with and could have been a great group of three.
And that Jla decided not to give us all that transition of: "i don't like you weirdo - hmm i think i like you - hey, i consider you something like a sister" bothers me because the author decided not to make those two the best friends they deserved to be.
And I think Jla did it because she realized that people ship Roth and Trinity, and she didn't want to hurt the Roth / Layla, Trinity / Zayne relationship. But JLA too late, because Layla and Zayne were irritating, you had to start there.

3. Dez
I liked Dez in his book, but him saying that he would risk his life for Zayne seemed very ???? BOY, YOU HAVE CHILDREN. YOU HAVE A WIFE. Why are you risking your life for Zayne? They weren't even close friends. If I were Jasmine, I would seriously leave you.
And the fact that Dez had a bigger role in this book and it was he who accompanied Trin on his journey to get Zayne back?
LOOOL. Are we going to pretend not to see what was going on here? Jla desperate to find a last minute friend as she sent Roth to hell ** suspicious ** and that Cayman couldn't ** suspicious x2**, just because the author didn't want some readers to keep shiping to Trinity with both boys and will they downplay Zayne.
So she had to go and find a married man with children to be Trin's friend and not-potential-boyfriend.
Well Jla, went wrong, because i have shipped them anyway.

4. Jada and all of Trin's friends.
Well, I hope her name was Jada or this will be awkward. But the fact that Jla liked isolating Trin and was practically just surrounded by Zayne's friends?
Nothing makes my hair stand on end more than a girl who only has her boyfriend's friends as friends. And much worse if your """two closest friends (layla and stacey)"" acted like bitches with you.
And two demons (cayman and roth) that could easily turn their backs if Layla is in danger?
Well that's not very reliable, is it?
I found it in bad taste that Jla didn't give Trin's friends more prominence in this book, at least. Jada appeared in a chapter and a half and that was it. I think Jada and Ty easily COULD HAVE ACCOMPANIED TRIN ON HIS TRIP. Yes, they should have. Or his adoptive parents. People who were trustworthy and loved Trin, not Zayne's friends.
Because really, let's imagine that in the future Zayne and Trin break up, do you really think that Trin is going to seek comfort from Layla or Stacey? Nope. She will say something like: "They were always friends with him and not mine." So hey, big failure there Jla.

5. Peanut, his ghost friend, turned out to be his father!!
God, define pathetic. Well then Peanut turned out to be her dad and it seems like Jla got that idea off her ass at the last minute because nothing fitted and at the same time "oh, it all fit" so pathetically. Also, Peanut used to spy on Zayne while he bathed and would make double-meaning comments about it.
Yes, we already know that you want your daughter's boyfriend.
We also know that Jla did not plan for you to be the father and that the girl who saw ghosts was going to have more prominence, but it turned out that she got bored at the last minute and was only interested in continuing with Casteel and what was the other girl's name? Penelope?

6.Trinity was unrecognizable. It wasn't the Trin that I liked in the previous books, it seemed muffled and dumber than usual.
I didn't like Zayne's change in attitude. Or rather, I loved it, that's how Zayne must have been from the start. Only then could i have believed that he loved and deserved Trin.
But at this point I don't like the change because I see it more as supernatural magic, I don't feel like it's the real Zayne. It's like when Layla took a piece of his soul away from him and it got nasty and everyone said, "that's not Zayne." Well, the same here. This is not Zayne. He is the Zayne he should have been, but not who he really was. And I can't like him if I feel like all this change has been false, pure supernatural power, and not a natural change of his. I feel like in this book the hero was his intense twin.

7. Layla's and her pathetic apologies, how stressful. Jla was able to go deeper there. Same with Stacey, and i don't like, but if she's your boyfriend's best friend, whom you'll have to see your whole life, at least you can spend a little time together to fix things before the book is over.
Jla really did give Zayne and Layla a couple cute moments for... what? Did anyone really want that friendship back? Okay, I don't judge you.
But she could also give me my Roth-Trin fuckin moments!!!

8. NOTHING happened in this book, seriously. The characters spent their time going from house to house, looking for people they would never find, having silly conversations (it improves your dialogues jla, you're not funny!), And embarrassing everyone by bringing a Lucifer who looked like my teenage cousin. Even Zayne and Trin's romantic moments were boring.

I forgot to say!! Danika is the best thing that ever happened to this world of guardians / demons but I really hope she never gets a book (too bad, she had potential) because Jla is capable of making her dumb and Nikolai could be a cry baby with no emotional responsibility and most likely: he would not yet get over his ex-wife and cruelly push Danika away. Oh, i can already feel it.
And another thing, i wish Zayne, Layla and Stacey had died.
Man, i wished Roth and Trinity fell in love so bad :( they seriously had potential. It's a shame.
And damn it, Jla, don't write another book about this world. Let them rest and dedicate yourself to your true passion: making Casteel steal the lines of your other heroes.


As Jla said in her thanks, it is bittersweet to end this series. And sis, you are right, it is so bittersweet to end this series because i ended up hating it very badly.
When I want to re-read the main trilogy (just to read some excerpts from Roth) I will remember this series and I will cry about how horrible it was.
That's it. I was ruined by beautiful memories of Roth.
Layla and Zayne were never important.
And I wish Trinity had been Roth's girlfriend, they had so much more potential and chemistry than the other two unsalted eggs.

An epic conclusion to an amazing trilogy.

Jen gave Zayne and Trinity and the whole Dark Elements/ Harbinger world a satisfying ending. I was worried going into reading this book that I wouldn’t connect with as much as I have been reading a lot of New Adult fantasy and going into a Young Adult urban fantasy was very different. But I forgot how much I love Jen’s urban fantasies, she included such funny banter between characters, great jokes about pop culture but also keeping on track with the whole ‘we need to save the world’ vibe.

After finishing Rage and Ruin and experiencing THAT cliff-hanger I knew this book would start off with some major stuff happening and I was not disappointed. The first ten chapters of the book you see Trinity and Zayne going through it. What they deal with and what they have to do was a shocker, I didn’t expect it to happen and it was nice that the story wasn’t solely focused on one storyline. Zayne and Trinity relationship was just the best in this book, they experienced some really cute moments, heart-stopping moments and some YA level spice that made me wish the book was in NA. they head to deal with this brand-new relationship while also figuring out how to save everyone. After finishing this trilogy Zayne and Trinity have become one of my favourite couples.

We of course got all best twists and reveals throughout the book. Especially in the last few chapters, some I didn’t expect. They kept me even more invested in this book and I couldn’t stop reading! Meeting Lucifer was one of the highlights of this book for me, he was such a funny character. He reminded me a lot of the TV show Lucifer in Lucifer. There were moments I laughed out loud and shock my head in disbelief at some of the things he said and did. He was great! As always, I loved seeing Roth, Layla and Caymen. They’re dynamic and what they add to the story was just great.

Throughout the books you see trinity living with her Retinitis Pigmentosa and adapting her fighting to work with it. One thing I loved is that Jen didn’t magically ‘cure’ Trinity’s RP through some angelic powers, she easily could of but didn’t. that made Trinity more real and I really liked how she did it. It showed that you can be a badass trueborn whatever genetic disease you have.

Overall, I absolutely loved this book. I am sad that the series is over and I have to say goodbye to the characters but I can always reread as much as I want! You guys with love Grace and Glory.

Il terzo e ultimo capitolo della trilogia di Tempesta e Furia non delude affatto.
Finalmente assistiamo alla "resa dei conti" con battaglia finale.
Gli stereotipi continuano? Abbastanza, ma non è questo il punto, perchè per quanto banale e prevedibile possa essere la vicenda, Armentrout ha un modo talmente coinvolgente e appassionante di raccontarla, che alla fine ti ritrovi a leggere alle due di notte nonostante la sveglia puntata presto per il mattino dopo (*ovviamente non è un fatto realmente accaduto*).
I personaggi, più boni e potenti che mai, risultano interessanti e, nonostante le premesse, hanno ancora tanto da dire.
Il finale, decisamente poco originale (ma ho amato il colpo di scena), è coerente con tutto il resto della narrazione e, personalmente, mi è piaciuto.
Nel complesso il ritmo serrato degli eventi rende questo terzo libro degno di essere letto.

Dando l'addio a Trinity e Zayne, mi sento di ribadire le mie impressioni iniziali: la Harbinger Series non è una trilogia imperdibile, ma è sicuramente una lettura simpatica e divertente che intrattiene moltissimo. Se avete bisogno di decomprimere dopo un periodo di letture pesanti è decisamente la trilogia che fa per voi.

E così arriviamo alla fine di un'altra trilogia...

Chi mi segue da un po' sa quanto io amassi Zayne già dalla Dark Elements, quindi per me la serie spin-off Harbinger è stata una delle gioie della vita.
Avere nuovamente una trilogia paranormal con il Guardiano del mio cuore protagonista, stavolta insieme a Trinity - la quale a mio parere tira fuori il meglio di lui -, con un nuovo nemico da sconfiggere e i vecchi protagonisti come personaggi secondari (ciao Roth, Layla, Cayman, Guardiani e i famigli di Roth!) mi ha portato ad amare l'intera trilogia.

Questo volume conclusivo mi è piaciuto da matti.
Dopo il finale praticamente illegale del secondo volume ero curiosa e anche un po' preoccupata di come la Armentrout avrebbe deciso di evolvere e concludere la storia e invece c'è riuscita senza perdere un colpo.

La prima parte del libro è la mia preferita: il cambiamento che viene affrontato dai personaggi si sente e ho adorato il modo in cui Zayne evolve.
Lo adoravo già prima ma questa versione di lui TOP. Mi mancava proprio una parte un po' più rude e, anche se un po' mi ricorda Roth, per me è approvatissima.
Trinity rientra fra le protagoniste che mi piacciono perchè per quanto caotica e ironica sia è anche forte, non si lascia abbattere dalla malattia e in generale va sempre avanti per la sua strada.

Il finale è stato perfetto.
Prevedibile per certi versi ma per altri secondo me no. Sulle ultime pagine, infatti, sono un po' rimasta a bocca aperta, non tanto per ciò che succede ma per il contesto in cui succede! Non me l'aspettavo e mi è piaciuto molto.
Belli anche i riferimenti a Supernatural (chi ha letto SA lol) e anche se a volte sono un po' overpowering comunque non mi sono dispiaciuti.

Mi mancheranno tanto tutti!

4'5 🌟 Tras leer el final de la segunda parte tenía millones de ganas de saber como terminaba esta historia pero a la vez no quería ponerme con ella porque me daba mucha pena tener que despedirme de los personajes 🙈 He tardado lo mío en leerlo, ha sido de los libros que más lento he leído, ya que he ido disfrutando de cada cosa que iba sucediendo porque esta novela tiene muchísima acción y giros inesperados. Para mí, ha sido un cierre perfecto para esta historia donde no tenía claro si Zayne me gustaría ya que no le tenía mucho cariño, no obstante, ahora me ha ganado aunque Trinity ha sido mi protagonista favorita y es que la autora ha creado un personaje fuerte y valiente que te deja huella. Jennifer L. Armentrout tiene la capacidad de crear historias que te atrapan y te dejan con ganas de más, cada una de las novelas que he leído de ella tienen algo especial y en todas me he encontrado con personajes que al final se han ganado mi corazón 😍 Sin lugar a dudas, leeré todos los libros de la autora y algún día seguro que releo la trilogía 💛


"Gracia Y Gloria" es la última entrega de la trilogía El Heraldo. El broche perfecto para una historia que desprende acción, secretos y giros inesperados en cada una de sus entregas. Una novela perfecta para a quienes le gusten las historias de guardianes, ángeles y demonios. Un libro que tiene una protagonista fuerte y valiente que adorarás 😍🌗💥🌠🧡

Ohh qué pena sientooo, se ha acabado. ¡Cómo he disfrutado esta trilogía! Ha sido una lectura estupenda.

Este libro comienza con sorpresa y de una manera apoteósica que casi me hizo leer medio libro de tirón y tiene casi 500 páginas eh? Muy a lo Armentrout todo hay que decirlo, esta autora es la caña. Para no variar con respecto a los otro títulos, en esta historia hay un poco de todo; humor, romance, intriga y misterio entre otros, por ello es una lectura muy completa.

En cuanto a los personajes puedo seguir asegurando que tanto Trinity como Zayne son unos personajes fantásticos, aunque destaco una milésima más a Trinity por lo divertida y desastre que es. Me encanta. En este libro conocemos al temido Lucifer que me ha hecho pasar muy buenos ratos.

Sé que después de leer esta magnífica trilogía caeré en un bloqueo increíble, voy a echar mucho de menos a Trinity, a Zayne y a todos los demás. Espero que la autora se anime y nos regale algo de Lucifer, sería estupendo.

Si quieres pasar un buen rato y sumergirte en una aventura sin igual este puede ser tu libro.
